text:
sam (monitoring): alert -> Okta token introspect /oauth2/v1/token and /v1/introspect returning 502/503 since 09:03 UTC. spike in failed logins and console auth errors. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/okta-auth failures
incidents-bot: New incident created: SEV2 - Okta API errors impacting logins (incident id: INC-20260715-01) :rotating_light:
alice (on-call): ack. i'm on it. pulling logs and confirming scope. @dana can you verify if we have a cached-jwks fallback ready?
sam (monitoring): alert detail: rate 503 = 18/min, avg latency to jwks endpoint 12s, tokens failing in frontend auth service with 504/timeout to okta.
alice (on-call): quick reproducer from prod edge (09:06):
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://login.okta.com/oauth2/v1/introspect -d 'token=xxxx' -H 'Authorization: Basic ***'
HTTP/2 503
server: nginx

```
cheng (prod-eng): seeing backend errors in verifier service: `error verifying token: fetch_jwks failed: context deadline exceeded` repeated across regions. stack traces show consistent timeout to `https://company.okta.com/.well-known/jwks.json`
dana (platform-sre): we have a soft fallback to cached JWKS for 60s in platform-config, but it's currently disabled for tokens >24h. i can push a config patch to increase jwks_cache_ttl to 300s and allow caching for all token ages. would reduce external calls.
alice (on-call): please push it. i'll coordinate deploy. 
DANA: rolling out patch to prod-apisets 09:12 UTC (patch id: pf-20260715-01). command: `rheld deploy --service auth-verifier --set jwks_cache_ttl=300`
alice (on-call): deploying config now -> started canary on us-east-1.
ben (on-call-next): i'm standing by for handoff, ETA 09:30 UTC. pls ping me when stable.
maria (support): customer impact snapshot at 09:18: 9 orgs reporting login failures, ~120 failed login attempts in last 15m, 2 enterprise customers blocked from console. CS contacting top accounts now.
okta-support-bot: Okta ticket OKTA-789012 opened with priority P1. Okta acknowledges elevated errors and investigating their edge cluster.
alice (on-call): can we temporarily allow console access via service tokens for affected enterprise customers? that's a manual opt-in but would mitigate console lockouts while upstream heals.
cheng (prod-eng): we can generate short-lived service tokens and scope them to console access for the 2 affected customers. need ops approval.
dana (platform-sre): approved. issuing tokens for customer A and B now. note: audit logs will record bypass.
incidents-bot: update: SEV2 -> mitigation in progress.
alice (on-call): monitoring: after config push started 09:12, 09:20 saw a drop in 5xx rate to 6/min, by 09:28 down to 1-2/min. still seeing occasional blips.
sam (monitoring): metric links: https://grafana.redwood/okta-auth?from=09:00&to=09:40 - look at `auth.verifier.jwks_fetch_failures`
ben (on-call-next): taking over paging at 09:30 UTC. alice -> i'll own the channel for the next 45m, please handover.
alice (on-call): handoff ack. summary for ben: incident INC-20260715-01, root cause: Okta edge returning 5xx/timeouts to jwks and introspect endpoints; mitigation: increased jwks_cache_ttl to 300s and enabled caching for all token ages; generated temporary service tokens for 2 enterprise customers for console access; Okta ticket OKTA-789012. keep monitoring for token rejections.
ben (on-call-next): noted. questions: any rollback needed?
alice (on-call): not needed; change is conservative. will keep traffic routing as-is.
maria (support): CS update sent to impacted accounts at 09:35 UTC, message includes workaround and expected timeline. requesting OOO/contact list for enterprise A & B in case we need to escalate.
okta-support-bot: Okta update 09:36 UTC: root cause identified as edge certificate reload issue causing node restarts; mitigation underway. approximate recovery ETA unknown.
cheng (prod-eng): proposed follow-ups: 1) postmortem to capture why our jwks fetch had no long-term cache fallback, 2) consider local JWKS refresher with backoff + disk-cache, 3) add synthetic checks for jwks latency on deploys.
incidents-bot: SLA watch enabled.
ben (on-call-next): monitoring shows auth failures now at baseline ~0.2% of logins for the last 10m, previous peak ~4%. i'll keep paging if it creeps.
alice (on-call): excellent. please file INC-REVIEW ticket and add timeline + customer impact. i'll join postmortem. :thumbsup:
ben (on-call-next): created postmortem ticket PM-20260715-01 and added initial timeline. assigning to alice + cheng + dana.
maria (support): closing customer notifications pending full resolution. will reopen if Okta reports regression.
incidents-bot: incident INC-20260715-01 moved to monitoring state at 09:58 UTC.
okta-support-bot: Okta resolved 10:02 UTC — they confirm edge cluster redistribution completed, normalizing traffic.
alice (on-call): marking mitigation success, will prepare RCA draft. thanks team for quick turnaround.
ben (on-call-next): ending shift handoff at 10:15 UTC. leaving monitoring on.
summary (alice): impact: temporary login failures and console lockouts for a small subset of customers due to Okta edge failures. mitigation: local caching and temporary tokens reduced customer-visible errors. next steps: RCA, add durable jwks cache, synth checks, and customer follow-up.
_meta: generated for dataset: slack incidents thread about third-party auth provider causing login/tokens failures
